explanation: Read the three snake rows directly from their index patterns: 1,5,9,...; 0,2,4,...; and 3,7,11,... . Every input character appears exactly once.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. The three disjoint index classes cover every character exactly once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) space for the output buffer. All n characters are stored in the output buffer; index counters are constant-size.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/snake_string.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: The top row consists exactly of indices congruent to 1 modulo 4, the bottom row of indices congruent to 3 modulo 4, and the middle row of even indices. These three disjoint index classes cover every character. Appending each class in increasing index order, from top row to bottom row, therefore produces exactly the required row-by-row reading.
walkthrough: For CedarTrail, the top row takes indices 1, 5, 9: eTl. The middle takes 0, 2, 4, 6, 8: Cdrri. The bottom takes 3, 7: aa. Concatenating the rows yields eTlCdrriaa.
edgeCases: Empty input produces an empty string.
Very short strings may leave one or both outside rows empty.
Spaces, punctuation and character case are preserved as ordinary characters.
Character positions in this implementation are UTF-8 bytes, not user-perceived grapheme clusters.
